processing_steps_notes.value: A 100 g alloy ingot was prepared by melting 99.99% pure iron, 99.9% pure manganese, 99.9% pure aluminum, 99.9% pure chromium and 99.8% high-purity graphite by a cold-crucible levitation melting setup (x=0 for the 0Cr steel).

processing_steps_notes.value: The ingot was remelted by induction melting and the molten metal was poured into a copper mold rotating at 600 rpm, yielding as-cast steel strips of 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm. The near-rapid solidification was carried out under an argon atmosphere at a cooling rate of 1–1 × 10^4 K/s.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the as-cast 0Cr steel strip (wt.%): Mn 20.43, Al 9.16, C 1.17, Cr 0, S 0.0006, Fe Bal. (Table 1).
The product of ultimate tensile strength and total elongation (UTS × TE) for the as-cast 0Cr steel strip is 34.0 GPa % (Table 2).
Measured lattice parameters in the as-cast 0Cr steel strip: κ-carbide = 0.387 nm and γ-austenite = 0.375 nm.

The ideal stoichiometry of the κ-carbide is (Fe, Mn)3AlC with a perovskite crystal structure; Fe or Mn atoms occupy the cornered positions, Al atoms occupy the face-center positions, and C is in the center of the cube (½, ½, ½).

The ordered DO3 phase in the ferrite is a body-centered cubic crystal with a lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm, in which Fe or Mn atoms occupy cornered positions and Al or Fe/Mn atoms occupy every other centered positions.

The annealing treatment increases the yield strength of 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr steel strips by 131 MPa, 277 MPa and 141 MPa respectively (cited increment for 0Cr = 131 MPa; concerns the annealed state, not the as-cast sample).
